title: Priority-aware multi-workload soak and burst harness for Dedicated autoscale
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable soak + burst test harness that exercises Dedicated GPU pools with mixed traffic profiles (steady-state + periodic burst), measures tokens/sec and request p95, and wires into the regression detector so we catch service-level performance regressions before rollouts.

Background: Current soak runs exercise single workload shapes and either long steady-state or short bursts. We need a single harness that can run multi-workload mixes (small chat requests, long-completion generation, and embeddings) concurrently against a Dedicated pool, capture TTL-aware KV cache warmup effects, and validate autoscale policies (scale-out/scale-in thresholds, cooldown). This ticket implements the harness, onboarding dashboards, and automated alerts for statistical regressions against a rolling baseline.

Scope:
- Traffic mixes: 60% interactive chat (avg 64 tokens), 30% long generations (avg 512 tokens), 10% embeddings.
- Two phases per run: 6h steady-state at target tokens/sec, then 30m controlled burst to 3x tokens/sec. Repeat for 3 cycles.
- Metrics to collect: aggregate tokens/sec, per-route p95 response latency, p50/p95 per-token latency, KV cache hit ratio, request queue length, GPU utilization, and autoscale events (scale decisions + time-to-scale).
- Regression detection: integrate with perf-regression-detector service. Use baseline of last 12 canonical runs, alert on >15% relative increase in p95 with p < 0.01 (bootstrap CI).
- Acceptance criteria:
  * Steady-state run meets target aggregate tokens/sec +/-10% for 80% of the steady window.
  * p95 request latency increase <= 10% vs baseline for steady-state.
  * Burst completes with autoscale responding within configured SLO (scale-up start within 60s of sustained CPU/GPU pressure; new capacity handling 2x request rate without >25% p95 degradation).
  * Regression detector integrated and firing automated JIRA/Github alerts when thresholds breached.

Implementation plan:
1) Load harness: extend benchmark-runner to support multi-workload mixes and dynamic traffic shaping. Implement traffic schedule DSL that describes phase durations, per-workload QPS, and burst multiplier.
2) Metrics and labeling: standardize tag schema (route, workload_type, test_run_id, pool_id) so Grafana Dashboard and regression detector can aggregate at the right granularity.
3) Cache warmup: add a warmup stage that replays a sample of common prefixes to simulate warmed KV caches; compare runs with/without warmup to quantify effect.
4) Autoscale observability: emit scale decisions to the metrics pipeline and correlate scale decisions with latency spikes in an analysis job.
5) Regression detector: add CI job that schedules harness runs nightly on staging Dedicated pools and records run snapshots to S3. Integrate with perf-regression-detector and add alert routing to #infra-perf and paging for P0s.
6) Dashboards and runbook: build Grafana panels for tokens/sec, p50/p95, cache hit rate, and autoscale event timeline; author runbook with diagnosis steps and mitigations.

Run parameters for first stable run (baseline):
- Pool: dedicated-staging-eu-west-1 (4 GPUs)
- Target steady-state aggregate tokens/sec: 9,000 tokens/sec (approx 540k tokens/min)
- Long gen requests: 512 tokens target, 30 RPS global
- Chat requests: 64 tokens target, 250 RPS global
- Embeddings: batch 64, 10 RPS global
- Run length: 6h steady-state + 3x(30m burst + 90m recovery)

Notes on measurement: p95 measured at request completion time (end-to-end), token latency reported per-token by runtime sampling. Use 95th-percentile computed across request-level latencies, and compute bootstrap CI for p95 as part of regression detection. Store raw histograms in metrics bucket for later analysis.

Out-of-scope: production Dedicated pools, user-visible routing changes, and long-term capacity planning beyond detection and reporting.
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Created ticket. Initial hypothesis: mixed traffic + cache warmup drives different autoscale behavior than our current single-workload soaks. Goal is an automated nightly run that integrates with regression detection.

2026-03-04 Sofia Martinez (PM): Design review - suggested adding priority-aware shaping so higher-paying customers' requests are represented during bursts. Requested we include a ’priority tier’ tag per request. Updated scope to include priority-aware traffic mix.

2026-03-06 Arjun Patel (Eng): Spike results attached to PR - early runs show KV cache warming reduces p95 by ~18% for long gen workload. Saved raw traces to s3://redwood-perf/soak/ENG-15432/spike1/. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-runner/pull/154

2026-03-08 Ethan Park (SRE): Reviewed autoscale observability instrumentation. Recommended emitting a 'scale_event_id' and 'scale_reason' labels to correlate metrics. Logged follow-up ENG-15455 for small agent-side patch.

2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Integrated perf-regression-detector. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-detector/pull/342. Detector uses last 12 runs as baseline and flags relative p95 regressions >15% with bootstrap p<0.01. Configured alert routing to #infra-perf and attached run to Grafana: grafana.redwood.io/d/dedicated/soak-15432

2026-03-12 QA run: Nightly run detected a transient p95 regression during first burst. Investigating cache warmup sequencing and priority-aware queueing; hypothesis: priority batching unintentionally increased latency for mid-tier requests. Created follow-up sub-issue ENG-15433 to adjust batching policy.

2026-03-14 Arjun Patel: Current status: harness core implemented, regression detector wired, dashboards in draft. Next steps: finalize priority shaping implementation, run three canonical baselines, and lock in acceptance criteria. Assigned to cycle 2026-W11 for final verification.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run full multi-workload scenario end-to-end and upload trace artifacts to S3
Grafana dashboard with tokens/sec, p50/p95, cache hit rate, GPU util, and autoscale timeline is available and linked from ticket
Regression detector fires alerts when p95 worsens >15% relative to baseline and posts an automated summary to #infra-perf
Three consecutive canonical runs (same parameters) produce p95 within 10% of baseline for steady-state and autoscale responds to bursts within configured SLO
